author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island’s congressional delegation is pressing the Federal Emergency Management Agency for records explaining its decision to deny a major-disaster declaration after the February blizzard.

Sens. Jack Reed and Sheldon Whitehouse and Reps. Seth Magaziner and Gabe Amo sent a letter seeking preservation and production of agency records, Rhode Island Current reported Monday. The lawmakers say the documentation is needed to understand how the request was evaluated.

The storm dropped more than three feet of snow in parts of the state, including a record 37.9 inches reported at T.F. Green Airport. State estimates put cleanup and damage at about $19 million, with costs divided between state and local governments.

FEMA has denied the aid request, and the agency’s administrator has said there is no new information to provide. The delegation’s request does not change the denial, but it could add public detail about the review and the financial burden Rhode Island communities say the storm created.
dek: Rhode Island’s congressional delegation is asking for FEMA records as it challenges the agency’s decision not to issue a major-disaster declaration after February’s blizzard.
headline: Rhode Island delegation demands records after FEMA denies blizzard aid
